title: Egoism and Altruism
summary: The individual as the proper beneficiary of his own action, against the demand that he live for others.

lessons.title: Who the action is for
lessons.objective: Name the individual himself as the proper beneficiary of his own action.

exercises.prompt: On this unit’s view, who is the proper beneficiary of a person’s own action?

choices.text: That person himself
Whoever has the greater need
The group he belongs to
No one; action should benefit nobody

feedback.note: Egoism here means the actor is the proper beneficiary of what he does. The gain is his to seek.

exercises.prompt: Match each idea to the person it treats as the proper beneficiary.

pairs.left: Egoism, as this unit uses it
A code that says live for others
The demand rejected here
pairs.right: Other people, as a moral duty to live for them

feedback.note: The split is about who is supposed to gain. Egoism names the actor. The opposed demand names others.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit’s claim about the beneficiary.

parts.text: The individual is the proper
of his own action.

feedback.note: Beneficiary means the person for whom the action is properly done. That person is the individual who acts.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that states who should gain.

feedback.note: The action belongs to him, and the proper gain belongs to him as well.

exercises.prompt: A carpenter builds a table and is paid for it. Who does this unit treat as the proper beneficiary of that work?

choices.text: The carpenter, as the person who acted
Only people who did not pay him
Nobody, because payment spoils the work
The trade as a whole, not the man

feedback.note: He did the work. He is the proper beneficiary of it, including the payment he earns.

exercises.prompt: What does beneficiary mean in this unit?

choices.text: The person for whom the action is properly done
The person who feels sorry for the actor
A referee who scores the action
A tool the actor happens to use

feedback.note: The word marks the intended moral recipient of the action, not a feeling or a gadget.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase to what it affirms.

pairs.left: Proper beneficiary
His own action
The individual
pairs.right: The person whose life the action serves

feedback.note: Three pieces lock together: a person, his deed, and himself as the one who should gain.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two blanks.

parts.text: He acts, and the proper beneficiary is
, not a demand that he live for

feedback.note: The positive claim and the rejection travel together: himself, not others as the ones he must live for.

exercises.prompt: Which statement matches this unit?

choices.text: A person is the proper beneficiary of what he does
A person may act only if someone else is the beneficiary
Action has no beneficiary at all
The beneficiary rotates by public vote each day

feedback.note: The unit’s title names egoism as the claim that the actor is the proper beneficiary.

exercises.prompt: Build the short claim.

feedback.note: The claim is aimed at the actor: you, not a stand-in, are the proper beneficiary.

lessons.title: The demand to live for others
lessons.objective: Identify the moral demand this unit rejects: that a person live for others.

exercises.prompt: What demand does this unit set egoism against?

choices.text: The demand that he live for others
The demand that he notice facts
The demand that he learn a skill
The demand that he rest when tired

feedback.note: The opposed demand is moral: live for others. It is not a demand to be awake to reality or to do competent work.

exercises.prompt: Complete the rejection.

parts.text: Egoism stands against the demand that he
for others.

feedback.note: The phrase is live for others: his life is treated as something owed to them.

exercises.prompt: Match each demand to how this unit treats it.

pairs.left: Live for others
Be the beneficiary of your own action
Treat your life as fuel for other lives

feedback.note: Living for others and being used as fuel for other lives are the demand this unit refuses.

exercises.prompt: A teacher says your studies count only when they help strangers, never when they help you. What is that?

choices.text: The demand that you live for others
A statement of egoism
A reminder that you exist
A description of a fair wage

feedback.note: If your own benefit is ruled out and only others count, the demand is the one this unit rejects.

exercises.prompt: Build the demand this unit rejects.

feedback.note: Three words name the demand: live for others. The unit is written against that demand.

exercises.prompt: Living for others, in this unit, means which of these?

choices.text: Treating other people as the ones your life is for
Trading value for value when both sides gain
Speaking politely to neighbors
Knowing where other people live

feedback.note: The demand is about the purpose of your life, not manners or mere knowledge of other people.

exercises.prompt: Fill the contrast.

parts.text: Not live for
, but be the beneficiary of your
action.

feedback.note: The no and the yes are one contrast: others are not the ones you must live for; your own action is properly for you.

exercises.prompt: Which slogan matches the demand this unit opposes?

choices.text: Your life is for other people
Your life is your own to live
You may keep what you earn
Look at what is in front of you

feedback.note: Your life is for other people is the demand. The unit takes the other side.

exercises.prompt: Match the saying to the side it takes.

pairs.left: I am the proper beneficiary of what I do
I must live for others
My action is properly for me
My days belong to whoever needs them

feedback.note: Two sayings keep the actor as beneficiary. Two hand his life to other people.

exercises.prompt: Build what the unit refuses.

feedback.note: The refusal is direct: he need not live for others. That is the negative half of the unit.

lessons.title: What altruism asks
lessons.objective: Describe altruism, in this contrast, as the code that makes others the beneficiary of one’s action.

exercises.prompt: In the contrast this unit draws, what does altruism ask?

choices.text: That others be the beneficiary of your action
That you be the beneficiary of your action
That no one benefit from anything
That you study mathematics

feedback.note: Altruism, set against egoism here, places the beneficiary outside the actor.

exercises.prompt: Match each name to the beneficiary it assigns.

pairs.left: Egoism
Altruism, in this contrast
The demand to live for others
pairs.right: Others, as the purpose of one’s life

feedback.note: The names pick different beneficiaries. Egoism picks the actor. Altruism, as opposed here, picks others.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast in one line.

parts.text: Altruism, in this unit, asks you to live for
rather than as the beneficiary of your own action.

feedback.note: The word that fills the blank is others. That is the ask.

exercises.prompt: A code says every personal gain is a moral failure, and only gains kept by other people count. Which side is that?

choices.text: The altruist side of this contrast
The egoist side of this contrast
Neither, because both sides ban gain
Both sides at once

feedback.note: Ruling out the actor’s gain and keeping only other people’s gain is the altruist demand in this unit.

exercises.prompt: Build the altruist assignment of the beneficiary.

feedback.note: That sentence states the altruist side: the beneficiary is relocated to others.

exercises.prompt: Which pairing is correct for this unit?

choices.text: Egoism for the actor; altruism for others as beneficiary
Egoism for others; altruism for the actor
Both names mean the actor must live for others
Neither name says anything about a beneficiary

feedback.note: Do not swap the names. Egoism keeps the beneficiary with the actor. Altruism moves it to others.

exercises.prompt: Name both sides.

parts.text: The actor as beneficiary is
. Others as the ones he must live for is

feedback.note: The two titles of the unit name the two assignments of the beneficiary.

exercises.prompt: Altruism, as drawn here, is not which of the following?

choices.text: A street map of a city
A moral demand about who should gain
The claim that one should live for others
The opposite of the actor as beneficiary

feedback.note: In this unit altruism is a moral demand, not a neutral fact about streets or tools.

exercises.prompt: Match the question to the altruist answer in this contrast.

pairs.left: Who should your action be for?
Whose life is the purpose?
What is refused by egoism?

feedback.note: Altruism answers the who-gains question by pointing away from the actor. Egoism refuses that answer.

exercises.prompt: Build the egoist reply to that ask.

feedback.note: The reply declines the altruist assignment. The actor does not take others as the purpose of his life.

lessons.title: Action and its proper gain
lessons.objective: Connect a concrete action to the person who properly gains from it, and reject handing that gain away as a duty.

exercises.prompt: Lena studies medicine because she wants the career and the knowledge. This unit says the proper beneficiary of that study is:

choices.text: Lena
Only future patients, never Lena
No one, because study is not an action
The hospital’s budget office alone

feedback.note: She is the one acting. She is the proper beneficiary of the studying, even if patients later gain too.

exercises.prompt: A rule says Lena’s study is moral only if she erases her own benefit. What does this unit say about that rule?

choices.text: It is the demand that she live for others
It is what egoism requires
It is a fact of anatomy
It is optional spelling advice

feedback.note: Erasing her benefit so that only others remain is the demand the unit stands against.

exercises.prompt: Match the action to the proper beneficiary on this unit’s terms.

pairs.left: You cook a meal you will eat
You earn a wage for your work
You practice a skill you chose

feedback.note: In each case the person who acts is the proper beneficiary of that action.

exercises.prompt: Complete the judgment.

parts.text: The proper gain of his work stays with
. Handing it away as a duty would be living for

feedback.note: Keeping the gain with the actor is the egoist claim. Giving it up as a duty is the opposed demand.

exercises.prompt: Build the line about earned pay.

feedback.note: Pay for his work is a gain of his action. This unit treats that gain as properly his.

exercises.prompt: Marco shares a tool with a friend because he wants to, and he still owns the tool. Does that by itself mean he lives for others?

choices.text: No. A chosen share is not the demand that his life be for others
Yes. Any benefit to a second person is altruism
Yes. Egoism forbids ever letting anyone else gain
Yes. Ownership itself is living for others

feedback.note: The rejected demand is that he live for others. A voluntary share, with his own life still his, is not that demand.

exercises.prompt: Which case is the demand this unit rejects?

choices.text: You are told your life is owed to other people as such
You eat lunch because you are hungry
You take a job because the work and the pay are yours
You read a book you chose

feedback.note: Hunger, chosen work, and chosen reading keep you as beneficiary. Being told your life is owed is the demand.

exercises.prompt: Sort each line.

pairs.left: I keep the fruit of my effort
My effort is owed away from me
I chose to give a gift and still live my life
pairs.right: Not the same as the rejected demand

feedback.note: The moral issue is whether his life is treated as owed. A chosen gift does not rewrite who he is living for.

exercises.prompt: Fill the principle applied to work.

parts.text: The worker is the proper
of the work he does.

feedback.note: Apply the same word used for action in general: the worker is the beneficiary of his work.

exercises.prompt: Build the applied claim.

feedback.note: Effort she performs is properly for her. That is the beneficiary claim in a concrete case.

lessons.title: Hold the contrast
lessons.objective: Keep egoism and the rejected demand distinct when the wording changes.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is egoism, as this unit states it?

choices.text: The individual is the proper beneficiary of his own action
The individual must live for others
The individual should benefit no one, including himself
The group is the proper beneficiary of his action

feedback.note: The first sentence is the unit’s positive claim. The others hand the benefit away or cancel it.

exercises.prompt: Someone rewords the rejected demand as: your days exist to be spent on other lives. What is that still?

choices.text: The same demand that he live for others
A new claim that he is the beneficiary
A statement about the length of a day
Egoism under another name

feedback.note: A change of wording does not change the demand. If his days are for other lives, he is told to live for others.

exercises.prompt: Match the rewording to the side it really takes.

pairs.left: I am the one my effort is for
My effort is for other people as a duty
The proper beneficiary is the actor
The proper beneficiary is anyone but the actor

feedback.note: Track who is named as beneficiary. That, not the decoration of the sentence, decides the side.

exercises.prompt: Complete both halves of the unit.

parts.text: Beneficiary: the
. Against: the demand that he live for

feedback.note: Hold both halves. The individual is the beneficiary, and the opposed demand is living for others.

exercises.prompt: Build the full contrast in short form.

feedback.note: For himself, not for others, is the whole contrast in five words.

exercises.prompt: A speaker says egoism means the actor must make others the purpose of his life. What is wrong with that?

choices.text: It swaps in the demand egoism rejects
Nothing. That is the unit’s definition
Only the spelling of egoism
It confuses egoism with the time of day

feedback.note: Making others the purpose of his life is the demand this unit sets egoism against, not the content of egoism.

exercises.prompt: Which pair is the unit’s own pairing?

choices.text: Egoism with the actor as beneficiary; altruism with living for others
Egoism with living for others; altruism with the actor as beneficiary
Both names mean living for others
Both names mean there is no beneficiary

feedback.note: Keep the pairing stable. Egoism is the actor’s side. Altruism is the live-for-others side of this unit.

exercises.prompt: Match the test question to the egoist answer.

pairs.left: Who properly gains from his action?
Must he live for others?
What is that no aimed at?

feedback.note: Three answers restate one unit: he is the beneficiary, he need not live for others, and that refusal targets the altruist demand.

exercises.prompt: Repair the swapped sentence.

parts.text: Egoism says the proper beneficiary is the
, not that he must live for others.

feedback.note: If a sentence names the crowd as the egoist beneficiary, it has the unit backwards. The actor is the one named.

exercises.prompt: You finish the unit. Which summary is accurate?

choices.text: He is the proper beneficiary of his own action, and he is not required to live for others
He must live for others, and he is not a beneficiary
Beneficiary is a word with no moral use
Egoism and altruism name the same demand

feedback.note: That summary is the unit: the individual as beneficiary, against the demand that he live for others.
